specs.name: current_time
specs.description:
Get the current date and time in a timezone. Use this whenever the answer
depends on today's date or the time of day.

timezone.description: IANA timezone name, for example America/Toronto or Asia/Kolkata.
timezone.title: Timezone

specs.name: update_plan
specs.description:
Show the user a checklist of the steps you are taking. Use it for tasks
that need three or more steps: call it before starting with the whole plan,
then again with the full updated list whenever a step's status changes.
Keep at most one step in_progress. Skip it for simple questions.

specs.name: web_search
specs.description:
Search the web. Returns titles, URLs and short snippets. Snippets are often
incomplete: use web_fetch on the most relevant URLs before relying on them.

topic.description: Use news for recent events and announcements.
topic.title: Topic

time_range.description: Only return pages published within this period.
time_range.title: Time Range

specs.name: web_fetch
specs.description:
Read a web page and return its main text as Markdown, with links. Use it
to read pages found with web_search or given by the user.

url.description: The full http(s) URL of the page to read.
url.title: Url

specs.name: record_observation
specs.description:
Record what a scheduled watch observed. Only use this when a scheduled
watch run asks you to. Call it once, with found=false if the target or value
could not be found.

input_schema.description: What a watch run saw. ``value`` is set when the extract is a number.
input_schema.title: Observation

specs.name: schedule_create
specs.description:
Propose a scheduled task or watch for the user to confirm.

Use kind=task with a prompt for recurring or one-time work ("every weekday at
8am summarize ..."), and kind=watch with a watch spec to monitor a value and
alert on a condition ("tell me when the fare drops under $1500"). Resolve
relative times ("tomorrow 8am") with current_time first, and give one-shot
times as ISO 8601 with an offset. The job stays inactive until the user
confirms it in the UI; tell the user what you proposed and the next run times
this tool returns.

Changed.description: The value moved by at least ``min_delta`` since the previous observation.
Changed.title: Changed

CronSchedule.description: Standard five-field cron, evaluated in local wall-clock time of ``timezone``.
CronSchedule.title: CronSchedule

IntervalSchedule.description: Every N seconds of elapsed time (daylight saving does not affect it).
IntervalSchedule.title: IntervalSchedule

WatchSpec.description: What to look at, what to extract, and when to raise an alert.

target.description: A URL, or a search query, describing where to look.
target.title: Target

extract.description: What to read from the target, e.g. 'lowest round-trip fare in CAD'.
extract.title: Extract

WatchSpec.title: WatchSpec

input_schema.description: The editable part of a job.

prompt.description: For tasks: what the agent should do.
prompt.title: Prompt

input_schema.title: JobSpec

specs.name: schedule_list
specs.description: List the user's scheduled tasks and watches with their status and next run.

specs.name: schedule_set_status
specs.description: Pause, resume or delete a scheduled job by id (see schedule_list).

status.description: active resumes a paused job; it cannot activate an unconfirmed one.
status.title: Status

specs.name: notify_me
specs.description:
Send the user a message by email and browser push, for example a summary
they asked to receive. It only reaches the user themselves and needs their
approval each time.

# Intermittent Fasting Offers No Clear Advantage
URL: https://www.medscape.com/viewarticle/intermittent-fasting-offers-no-clear-advantage-2026a10005s7

Can intermittent fasting help people who have overweight lose weight? It is likely that intermittent fasting is not superior to other diets for weight loss and may not lead to higher quality of life, according to a Cochrane review now published by Luis Ignacio Garegnani of the University Institute of the Italian Hospital, Buenos Aires, Argentina, and colleagues. Garegnani and his team [analyzed](https://www.cochranelibrary.com/cdsr/doi/10.1002/14651858.CD015610.pub2/full) 22 randomized controlled trials.

The studies were evaluated according to two questions:

- Is intermittent fasting more effective for adults with overweight and [obesity](https://emedicine.medscape.com/article/123702-overview) than conventional dietary recommendations?
- How does intermittent fasting affect quality of life, diabetes status, blood [lipids](https://emedicine.medscape.com/article/2500032-overview), and adverse events?

“Intermittent fasting” groups together different eating approaches that divide time into regular eating and fasting periods, including variants such as alternate-day fasting, early and late time-restricted eating, one-meal-a-day and 5:2 fasting. The fasting and eating periods can vary greatly depending on the method.

## The Cochrane Review

“Previous meta-analyses with other or similar inclusion criteria have consistently found no advantage of intermittent fasting compared with comparable dietary interventions of similar calorie reduction. The Cochrane review therefore fits the existing picture,” Stefan Kabisch, study physician in the Clinic for Endocrinology and Metabolic Medicine at the German Center for Diabetes Research (DZD), Campus Benjamin Franklin, Charité — Berlin University Medicine, Berlin, Germany, told the Science Media Center. He said the hype surrounding intermittent fasting has never been supported by convincing human studies but rather was premature and unjustified. Even in Germany, a recommendation was issued prematurely, one that was not based on high-quality study data.

The review provides evidence that intermittent fasting appears to be similarly effective for weight loss in people with overweight and obesity as other dietary approaches. “But to be clear: so far these are indications, not proof,” said Jörg Meerpohl, director of the Institute for Evidence in Medicine at University Medical Center Freiburg, Freiburg, Germany, and director of Cochrane Germany.

## Intermittent Fasting

The selected studies are “extremely heterogeneous,” emphasized Annette Schürmann, spokesperson and board member of the DZD and former head of the Department of Experimental Diabetology at the German Institute of Human Nutrition Potsdam-Rehbrücke, Nuthetal, Germany. She said she was a bit disappointed by the review because she had hoped it would provide a clearer summary of the evidence on intermittent fasting. It appears the review authors wanted to promote the idea that intermittent fasting is not a good strategy for weight loss and health.

“Intermittent fasting does lead to a statistically significant weight loss. In the six studies evaluated for claim 2, intermittent fasting resulted in approximately 3.4% greater weight loss than the control group achieved. That is clinically significant — for example, UK NICE guidelines consider 3% meaningful, while US guidelines use 5% as a benchmark,” explained Leonie Heilbronn, head of the Obesity and Metabolism research group at the School of Medicine, College of Health, Adelaide University, Adelaide, Australia.

If the goal is substantial weight loss — for example, 20%-30% — intermittent fasting is not sufficient, Schürmann noted. Intermittent fasting generally achieves only 3%-7% body-weight loss, which can nevertheless be health-relevant. “If a more ambitious goal is sought, medical or surgical therapy is required,” Schürmann emphasized. Still, the statement that “intermittent fasting has no effect on weight loss” cannot simply be made. A 3% loss in body weight is not trivial and can have a very positive effect on blood pressure and glucose metabolism, she said.

Animal studies using [obese](https://emedicine.medscape.com/article/123702-overview), diabetes-prone models have shown that an intermittent fasting diet can have a positive effect on the pancreatic islets of Langerhans and thus on blood glucose levels, even if the animals make up for it during the eating window and consume as much as their obese control group, which was not subject to an intermittent fasting diet. “We cannot test that in humans, but it is reasonable to assume the findings are transferable,” Schürmann said. For that reason, an intermittent fasting diet could be particularly interesting for patients with prediabetes.

*This story was translated from Medscape’s German edition.*
